dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory
dossier_meta.statement_text: Question For every $ d $ does there exists a $ g $ such that every graph with average degree smaller than $ d $ and girth at least $ g $ has a matching-cut?
dossier_meta.context_text: Let $ G=(V,E) $ be a graph. A matching $ M $ is a matching-cut if there exists a set $ S\subset V $ such that $ M = E(S:V\setminus S) $ . Graphs having a matching-cut are called decomposable. It is known that every graph with $ |E| < 3(|V|-1)/2 $ is decomposable [BFP11].
dossier_meta.references_text:
- [C84] V. Chvátal, Recognizing decomposable graphs, J Graph Theory 8 (1984), 51–53
- [BFP11] P. Bonsma, A. Farley, A. Proskurowski, Extremal graphs having no matching cuts, J Graph Theory (2011)
